fruits.extendedStory: This great fortress was raised in 1204 by Meiler Fitzhenry, on the orders of King John of England. For a very long time its story kept turning. After the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921, the castle was handed to a new Provisional Government led by Michael Collins. Walk up to its walls and imagine both those days.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Diese große Festung wurde 1204 von Meiler Fitzhenry im Auftrag von König Johann von England errichtet. Sehr lange Zeit wandelte sich hier die Geschichte immer wieder. Nach dem Anglo-Irischen Vertrag von 1921 ging die Burg an eine neue Provisorische Regierung unter Michael Collins über. Geh zu den Mauern hinauf und stell dir beide Tage vor.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This great fortress was raised in 1204 by Meiler Fitzhenry, on the orders of King John of England. For a very long time its story kept turning. After the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921, the castle was handed to a new Provisional Government led by Michael Collins. Walk up to its walls and imagine both those days.

localizedStory.de: Blick hinauf zu dieser großen Festung, 1204 auf Befehl von König Johann von England errichtet.
localizedStory.en: Look up at this great fortress, raised in 1204 on the orders of King John of England.

fruits.name: Dublin Castle
fruits.story: Look up at this great fortress, raised in 1204 on the orders of King John of England.

fruits.extendedStory: When it opened in 1816, walking across cost money. Everyone who wanted to reach the far bank handed over a halfpenny to get there. Dubliners shortened that coin to a ha'penny, and the nickname stuck fast to the crossing. The charge was dropped in 1919, but by then nobody was going to call it anything else.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Als sie 1816 eröffnet wurde, kostete der Weg hinüber Geld. Wer ans andere Ufer wollte, legte zuerst einen halben Penny hin. Die Leute machten daraus einen Ha'penny, und der Spitzname blieb am Übergang hängen. 1919 fiel die Gebühr weg, doch da nannte sie ohnehin niemand mehr anders.
localizedExtendedStory.en: When it opened in 1816, walking across cost money. Everyone who wanted to reach the far bank handed over a halfpenny to get there. Dubliners shortened that coin to a ha'penny, and the nickname stuck fast to the crossing. The charge was dropped in 1919, but by then nobody was going to call it anything else.

localizedStory.de: Überquere die Brücke, deren Name an den halben Penny erinnert, den man einst fürs Überqueren zahlte. Die Maut fiel 1919 weg.
localizedStory.en: Long ago you dropped a ha'penny in a box just to walk across this little bridge. That toll stopped in 1919.

fruits.name: Ha'penny Bridge
fruits.story: Long ago you dropped a ha'penny in a box just to walk across this little bridge. That toll stopped in 1919.

fruits.extendedStory: It rises over Parliament Square, and you see the top of it long before you reach the foot. The architect Charles Lanyon shaped the tower, and the stonework was finished in 1853. Thirty and a half metres carries it clear above everything around it. It is a gate tower, so the way through runs right beneath the stone.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Er ragt über den Parliament Square, und man sieht seine Spitze lange vor dem Fuß. Der Architekt Charles Lanyon entwarf den Turm, das Mauerwerk war 1853 fertig. Dreißigeinhalb Meter heben ihn klar über alles ringsum hinaus. Es ist ein Torturm, der Weg führt also mitten unter dem Stein hindurch.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It rises over Parliament Square, and you see the top of it long before you reach the foot. The architect Charles Lanyon shaped the tower, and the stonework was finished in 1853. Thirty and a half metres carries it clear above everything around it. It is a gate tower, so the way through runs right beneath the stone.

localizedStory.de: Blick hinauf zu diesem hohen Turm, 30,5 Meter hoch, 1853 vom Architekten Charles Lanyon erbaut.
localizedStory.en: Look up at this tall tower, 30.5 metres high, built in 1853 by the architect Charles Lanyon.

fruits.name: Campanile
fruits.story: Look up at this tall tower, 30.5 metres high, built in 1853 by the architect Charles Lanyon.

fruits.extendedStory: The church was begun in 1825 and carries the name of Mary. Its style is neoclassical: the builders looked back to ancient Greece and Rome for their shapes. So the front is all straight columns and calm, level lines, with nothing fussy about it. From the street it reads more like a temple than a church.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Kirche wurde 1825 begonnen und trägt den Namen Marias. Ihr Stil ist klassizistisch: Die Baumeister schauten für ihre Formen zurück nach Griechenland und Rom. Deshalb ist die Front lauter gerade Säulen und ruhige, waagerechte Linien. Von der Straße wirkt sie eher wie ein Tempel als wie eine Kirche.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The church was begun in 1825 and carries the name of Mary. Its style is neoclassical: the builders looked back to ancient Greece and Rome for their shapes. So the front is all straight columns and calm, level lines, with nothing fussy about it. From the street it reads more like a temple than a church.

localizedStory.de: Tritt vor diese Kirche von 1825, im ruhigen, geordneten klassizistischen Stil erbaut.
localizedStory.en: Step up to this church from 1825, built in the calm, orderly neoclassical style.

fruits.name: Saint Mary's Cathedral
fruits.story: Step up to this church from 1825, built in the calm, orderly neoclassical style.

fruits.extendedStory: Hugh Lane, a sharp-eyed art collector, gave this gallery both its name and its founding collection. The idea took shape in 1908, and the doors of this building opened in 1933. Lane himself never saw it, for he was lost in 1915 when the RMS Lusitania went down. Still, the modern art he championed has drawn visitors here ever since.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Galerie ist nach Hugh Lane benannt, dem Mann, der sie gegründet hat. Ihre Geschichte begann 1908, und in diesem Gebäude öffnete sie 1933. Ihr Gründer erlebte diesen Tag leider nicht mehr, denn er kam 1915 an Bord der RMS Lusitania ums Leben. Doch die Galerie, von der er träumte, empfängt seither ihre Besucher.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Hugh Lane, a sharp-eyed art collector, gave this gallery both its name and its founding collection. The idea took shape in 1908, and the doors of this building opened in 1933. Lane himself never saw it, for he was lost in 1915 when the RMS Lusitania went down. Still, the modern art he championed has drawn visitors here ever since.

localizedStory.de: Tritt ein in die weltweit erste bekannte öffentliche Galerie für moderne Kunst.
localizedStory.en: Long before other cities dared, this place hung bold new paintings for everyone to see. A collector named Hugh Lane made it happen.

fruits.name: Hugh Lane Gallery
fruits.story: Long before other cities dared, this place hung bold new paintings for everyone to see. A collector named Hugh Lane made it happen.

fruits.extendedStory: Mary Mercer, who founded a hospital, was buried on this ground. So was the philosopher Francis Hutcheson. Their graves are gone from view now, but the names stayed with the place. The square itself is named for Theobald Wolfe Tone, who was baptised in the church that once stood here. Since 2003 a sculpture by Jackie McKenna has stood among the trees, called 'Ag Crú na Gréine'.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Mary Mercer, die ein Krankenhaus gründete, wurde auf diesem Boden begraben. Auch der Philosoph Francis Hutcheson. Ihre Gräber sind heute nicht mehr zu sehen, die Namen aber blieben dem Ort. Der Platz selbst ist nach Theobald Wolfe Tone benannt, der in der Kirche getauft wurde, die einst hier stand. Seit 2003 steht zwischen den Bäumen eine Skulptur von Jackie McKenna mit dem Titel 'Ag Crú na Gréine'.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Mary Mercer, who founded a hospital, was buried on this ground. So was the philosopher Francis Hutcheson. Their graves are gone from view now, but the names stayed with the place. The square itself is named for Theobald Wolfe Tone, who was baptised in the church that once stood here. Since 2003 a sculpture by Jackie McKenna has stood among the trees, called 'Ag Crú na Gréine'.

localizedStory.de: Dieser grüne Park war einst der Friedhof von St Mary's und wurde 1966 als offene Wiese neu angelegt.
localizedStory.en: This green park was once the graveyard of St Mary's, laid out fresh as open lawn in 1966.

fruits.name: Wolfe Tone Square
fruits.story: This green park was once the graveyard of St Mary's, laid out fresh as open lawn in 1966.

fruits.extendedStory: Look carefully at the year this crossing was built, back in 1932. It was a big year for Dublin. The city hosted the great Eucharistic Congress, a huge gathering of people. That is why the bridge also carries an Irish name, Congress Bridge. Two names, and both remember the very same year.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Sieh dir genau das Baujahr dieser Brücke an, 1932. Es war ein großes Jahr für Dublin. Die Stadt war Gastgeber des großen Eucharistischen Kongresses, einer riesigen Versammlung von Menschen. Darum trägt die Brücke auch einen irischen Namen, Congress Bridge. Zwei Namen, und beide erinnern an dasselbe Jahr.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Look carefully at the year this crossing was built, back in 1932. It was a big year for Dublin. The city hosted the great Eucharistic Congress, a huge gathering of people. That is why the bridge also carries an Irish name, Congress Bridge. Two names, and both remember the very same year.

localizedStory.de: Diese Brücke ist nach Isaac Butt benannt, einem Anführer der irischen Home-Rule-Bewegung.
localizedStory.en: This bridge is named after Isaac Butt, a leader of Ireland's Home Rule movement.

fruits.name: Butt Bridge
fruits.story: This bridge is named after Isaac Butt, a leader of Ireland's Home Rule movement.

fruits.extendedStory: It opened in 1881 under a different name, the South City Markets. Fire gutted the building in 1892, and Dublin put it back together. The doors opened again in 1894, and traders have kept them open since. The style is Victorian, so look up at the ironwork and the long roof over the aisles.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Eröffnet wurde es 1881 unter einem anderen Namen, den South City Markets. 1892 brannte das Gebäude aus, und Dublin baute es wieder auf. 1894 öffneten die Türen erneut, und seither halten Händler sie offen. Der Stil ist viktorianisch, schau nach oben auf das Eisenwerk und das lange Dach über den Gängen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It opened in 1881 under a different name, the South City Markets. Fire gutted the building in 1892, and Dublin put it back together. The doors opened again in 1894, and traders have kept them open since. The style is Victorian, so look up at the ironwork and the long roof over the aisles.

localizedStory.de: Tritt ein in Dublins erstes eigens gebautes viktorianisches Einkaufszentrum, 1881 als South City Markets eröffnet.
localizedStory.en: Under this roof, traders have sold their wares since 1881, when it first threw open its doors.

fruits.name: George's Street Arcade
fruits.story: Under this roof, traders have sold their wares since 1881, when it first threw open its doors.

fruits.extendedStory: The diamond is old. It is already drawn on Thomas Campbell's map of 1811, before the Ordnance Survey had mapped this part of the city. The street beside it went by another name then, Gloucester Street, and kept it until 1933. In September 1981 hundreds of people who grew up around the crossing came back for a festival called Diamond Remembered.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Raute ist alt. Schon auf Thomas Campbells Karte von 1811 ist sie eingezeichnet, bevor die Ordnance Survey diesen Teil der Stadt vermaß. Die Straße daneben hieß damals anders, Gloucester Street, und blieb es bis 1933. Im September 1981 kamen Hunderte, die an dieser Kreuzung aufgewachsen waren, zu einem Fest namens Diamond Remembered zurück.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The diamond is old. It is already drawn on Thomas Campbell's map of 1811, before the Ordnance Survey had mapped this part of the city. The street beside it went by another name then, Gloucester Street, and kept it until 1933. In September 1981 hundreds of people who grew up around the crossing came back for a festival called Diamond Remembered.

localizedStory.de: Steh an dieser rautenförmigen Kreuzung, Mitte des 20. Jahrhunderts ein lebhafter Mittelpunkt für Straßenfußball.
localizedStory.en: Stand at this diamond-shaped crossing, a lively centre for street football back in the mid-20th century.

fruits.name: Gloucester Diamond
fruits.story: Stand at this diamond-shaped crossing, a lively centre for street football back in the mid-20th century.
